doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

chapter: Early road bands and the Army
title: Three weeks on tenor with Charlie Barnet
summary: His first name band was Barnet's, on tenor, with bandmates, then a summer at Lake Tahoe at low pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Charlie Barnet, was that your first name thing?

Yes. That was very short. That was three weeks. But he was my first name band affiliation. And there was one chair open on that band and a friend of mine said, “why don’t you try and go on this tour with us, it’ll be a start and you’ll meet some people” and so forth. So it was the fourth tenor chair, and I bought a tenor and I didn’t — I’ve never had an affinity for the tenor. I’ve never even taken the time to find a decent mouthpiece until a few years ago, and then my tenor got run over by a TWA baggage cart and that was the end of that. And actually it was a tenor that Willie Maiden who was on Maynard’s band with me had willed to me and it was a Vintage Mark VI. And I still have it and one day will get it fixed, but I don’t like to play tenor. But I did in that band. There © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

was probably nobody that you would know — well maybe there was, Gary Frummer played drums, who later played with Art Pepper and Chet Baker, and bass player named Don Payne who moved to New York and went on to do some Brazilian type things. There was a tenor player, a wonderful tenor player named Charlie Deremal, who had taken Ted Nash’s place with the original Billy May band, and he was a monster. And later for some reason he switched to alto for a while and played lead with Stan Kenton’s band, which I still can’t understand. But I don’t think there’s anybody else that you would know there. But it was just a three week thing. And a piano player named Ike Carpenter who you may have heard of, who had a band, a real screaming band out here for a lot of years, played piano in Charlie’s band and at the end of the three weeks Charlie took sort of the nucleus of the guys that wanted to go of that band up to Lake Tahoe and we stayed there for the summer, for three months, at the Calvada which was right up from the Cal Neva. I don’t know if you’re familiar with Lake Tahoe or not. But that was a nice little gig. It only paid $120 a week and you had to pay for your own lodging and food. So the only thing that happened from that, rewarding, for me, was that I found a dentist up there and had all the work done on my teeth and I came home with oh I don’t know $150 I guess.
